freeCopyCases: Physician or other owner: records free when the patient is referred to another provider for continuation of treatment (44-115-80(B))
Health care facility or Title 40 licensed provider: no fee for records sent to a provider at the patient's request for continuing medical care (44-7-325(A)(2))
feeRules: 44-115-80(A)(2) and 44-7-325(A)(1)(b): "sixty-five cents per page for the first thirty printed pages and fifty cents per page for all other printed pages, plus a clerical fee not to exceed twenty-five dollars for searching and handling"; paper cap $200 per request (physicians) or per admission (facilities)
Electronic copies: same per-page rates and clerical fee, capped at $150 per request (44-115-80(A)(1), 44-7-325(A)(1)(a))
Search fee may not be charged when no record is found if the patient made the request
All fees adjusted each July 1 by CPI-U South Region
X-ray copies: actual cost of reproduction only (44-115-80(C), 44-7-325(A)(3))

provisions.title: Physicians' Patient Records Act: fees physician may charge
provisions.quote: must provide a patient's medical records at no charge when the patient is referred by the physician, health care provider, or an employee, agent, or contractor of the owner of the record to another physician or health care provider for continuation of treatment
provisions.appliesTo: A physician, health care provider, or other owner of medical records

provisions.title: Fee for search and duplication of medical record; time limits
provisions.quote: no fee may be charged for records copied at the request of a health care provider or for records sent to a health care provider at the request of the patient for the purpose of continuing medical care
provisions.appliesTo: A health care facility, as defined in Section 44-7-130, and a health care provider licensed pursuant to Title 40

provisions.title: Health care facility deadline to comply with a copy request
provisions.quote: no later than forty-five days after the patient has been discharged or forty-five days after the request is received, whichever is later
provisions.appliesTo: A health care facility shall comply with a request for copies of a medical record

copy_rights.note: Free copy for continuing care counts; HIPAA has no such free case. The 45-day facility deadline is longer than 30 days and does not count. Per-page caps are facts only.

provisions.title: Abortions must be reported
provisions.quote: The names of the patient and physician may not be reported on the form or otherwise disclosed to the State Registrar.
provisions.appliesTo: Any abortion performed in this State must be reported by the performing physician

reproductive.note: Abortion reports to the State Registrar must omit patient and physician names. Section 44-41-360 also lets courts seal records to keep a patient's identity from public disclosure in actions under that article.

crossCheck.note: 44-41-60, history ends 2023 Act No. 70, eff May 25, 2023. 44-41-360 lets a court seal records to keep the patient's identity from public disclosure.

provisions.title: Confidentiality of records; exceptions; violations and penalties
provisions.quote: must be kept confidential, and must not be disclosed unless:
provisions.appliesTo: Certificates, applications, records, and reports made for the purpose of this chapter

mental_health.note: Records identifying a mental health or substance use patient need consent or a listed exception, such as a court order. Violation is a misdemeanor. Section 44-22-90 makes therapist communications privileged.

crossCheck.note: 44-22-100(A), last amended by 2013 Act No. 22, eff August 1, 2013. Agency names were updated by Code Commissioner under 2025 Act No. 3, not by amendment.

provisions.title: Confidentiality of sexually transmitted disease records
provisions.quote: relating to a known or suspected case of a sexually transmitted disease are strictly confidential except as provided in this section. The information must not be released or made public, upon subpoena or otherwise
provisions.appliesTo: All information and records held by the Department of Health and Environmental Control and its agents

hiv.note: Covers state health department STD records, with HIV named in the section. Section 44-29-136 requires a court order for release to prosecutors. Section 44-29-250 keeps anonymous HIV test results confidential.

crossCheck.note: 44-29-135, eff June 7, 2011, names HIV in item (f). 44-29-136 requires a court order for release to prosecutors. 44-29-250 makes anonymous HIV test results confidential.

provisions.title: Genetic information: confidentiality; disclosure restrictions and exceptions
provisions.quote: All genetic information obtained before or after the effective date of this chapter must be confidential and must not be disclosed to a third party in a manner that allows identification of the individual tested without first obtaining the written informed consent of that individual
provisions.appliesTo: This chapter applies to health insurance coverage offered in connection with an individual health plan, a group health plan, or a health benefit plan that is delivered, issued for delivery, or renewed in this State.

genetic.note: Chapter 38-93 sits in the Insurance title and applies to health insurance coverage, producers and insurance support organizations.

crossCheck.note: 38-93-40(A), 2010 Act No. 217, eff June 7, 2010. Chapter scope under 38-93-20 is health insurance coverage, producers, agencies and insurance support organizations.

facts.statutoryDamages: None fixed. Breach: damages for wilful and knowing violations, actual damages for negligent ones, injunction, attorney's fees. Genetic: equitable relief and actual damages, costs and attorney's fees.

provisions.title: Breach of security of business data: civil action by injured resident
provisions.quote: institute a civil action to recover damages in case of a wilful and knowing violation
provisions.appliesTo: A resident of this State who is injured by a violation of this section

provisions.title: Genetic information privacy: violations
provisions.quote: An individual who is injured by a person's violation of this chapter may recover in a court of competent jurisdiction the following remedies
provisions.appliesTo: This chapter applies to health insurance coverage offered in connection with an individual health plan, a group health plan, or a health benefit plan that is delivered, issued for delivery, or renewed in this State.

private_right.note: Suits allowed for breach notice violations and for genetic information violations in health insurance. No general right to sue found in the medical records acts (44-115, 44-22-100, 44-29-135).

crossCheck.note: Suits allowed under 39-1-90(G), a breach law, eff April 23, 2013, and 38-93-90(D), genetic information in insurance, eff June 7, 2010. Both are narrow. No general right found in 44-115 or 44-7.

facts.noticeDeadline: in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay

provisions.title: Business data, breach of security: definition of personal identifying information
provisions.quote: means the first name or first initial and last name in combination with and linked to any one or more of the following data elements
provisions.appliesTo: A person conducting business in this State, and owning or licensing computerized data or other data that includes personal identifying information

breach_health.note: Listed elements are SSN, license or state ID, financial account data and government identifiers. No medical or health insurance data. Consumer Affairs notice needed above 1,000 persons. Only GLBA and financial institutions get deemed compliance.

crossCheck.note: 39-1-90(D)(3), rewritten by 2013 Act No. 15, eff April 23, 2013, lists SSN, license, financial and government ID data only. Consumer Affairs notice above 1,000 persons. No HIPAA deeming clause.
